newsitem.title: USA: Kodak says in talks to make film in China.
newsitem.headline: Kodak says in talks to make film in China.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co on Tuesday said it was in talks with the Chinese government to make film and paper in China.
The company would not provide any details.

"We have not made any announcement. We have had discussions with the central government (of China). We have talked to people on all levels of the goverment but we are not in a position to comment," said Kodak spokesman Paul Allen.

"We have indicated that China was a high priority," he said, but declined to comment on the specific nature of talks. He would not say whether the company was exploring manufacturing film and paper in China for sale on the mainland or worlwide. "We are not in a position to comment," he said.
Meanwhile, Kodak shares rose 5/8 to 77-1/2 after a report that the company was in talks with several Chinese photo companies appeared in this morning's Wall Street Journal.
Jeffrey Pittsburg of Goldis-Pittsburg said he attributed the increase in Kodak's share price to the report.
"They are looking to have production facilities in China. They can make film cheaper," said Pittsburg. "People are reacting to a cost cutting measure."
Allen said he would have no comment on Kodak's stock price.
